thread:
incident-bot: Pager: High error rate from eu-west-1 for embeddings requests (alert: fallback-loop-high-5xx) :rotating_light:

carol (support): seeing multiple customers open tickets, says search embeddings failing with 500s and degraded latency.

sara (oncall): I'm oncall, acknowledging. Investigating routing/fallback policies now.

matt (eng-runtime): i can already see routing traces — several embed requests pinned to alias 'prod-v202' are being routed to the chat-compatible variant (instruct-chat-256q) after fallback. chat variant rejects tensor dims -> 500.

sara (oncall): that matches support reports. is this a pin mismatch or a policy misconfig?

matt (eng-runtime): looks like a pinned version alias was updated in the alias map last deploy. alias -> anchor points to v202 (embed-quant), but the fallback policy has a stale compatibility matrix that lists v202 as chat-compatible.

jess (eng-sre): logs snippet from the router (redacted):

```
2026-02-17T14:12:02Z router: req_id=abc123 alias=prod-v202 interface=embeddings route=eu-west-1->v202 fallback=allowed
2026-02-17T14:12:02Z router: decision=fallback target=instruct-chat-256q reason=capacity_shortage
2026-02-17T14:12:02Z runtime: dispatch failed: incompatible_interface (embeddings -> chat) code=INCOMPATIBLE_SCHEMA
2026-02-17T14:12:02Z runtime: responding 500 to client req_id=abc123
```

matt (eng-runtime): the fallback policy uses 'compatible_variant' flag which was not updated during the alias promotion. It thinks instruct-chat-256q is safe.

omar (product): any customer-visible mitigation we can do quickly?

sara (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) turn off automatic fallback-to-variant for alias prod-v202 in eu-west-1 (hot switch) 2) add a temporary routing rule to return 503 with friendly message instead of routing to incompatible variant 3) notify customers.

matt (eng-runtime): i can flip the fallback flag to false for that alias now. doing step 1.

incident-bot: Action: ToggleFallback(prod-v202, eu-west-1) requested by matt. executed at 2026-02-17T14:16:05Z.

matt (eng-runtime): done. fallback disabled for prod-v202 in eu-west-1. 

jess (eng-sre): pushing policy change to router to prefer 'no-fallback' when interface mismatch risk detected. will roll within 2 mins.

carol (support): sending customer note: "We're investigating intermittent 500s for embeddings in EU region; temporary protection in place; engineers rolling a fix."

omar (product): customer impact estimate?

sara (oncall): initial measurement: ~22k failed embedding requests in the window 14:10-14:22 UTC, affecting 3 enterprise customers (search indexer jobs). Error rate peaked at 28% for EU traffic.

matt (eng-runtime): also noting some cold-start capacity shortfalls triggered fallback attempts — we should patch autoscaler thresholds for embed pools.

jess (eng-sre): rolling change complete. router will now return 503 and route-only-to-compatible when fallback would cross interface.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigation applied. customer-facing incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1789997770 (draft)

carol (support): updated tickets with ETA and workaround: re-run indexer jobs with smaller batch size or route to us-east-1 for now.

omar (product): action items to follow-up in postmortem: - audit alias promotions to ensure compatibility matrix updated - add safe-guard in canary deploys to detect interface incompatibility - autoscaler tuning for embed pools - improved customer-facing error message when interface mismatch detected

sara (oncall): timeline note: root cause identified as stale compatibility metadata attached to alias promotion (release automation). rollback of alias wasn't needed thanks to fallback off, but we need to fix the automation.

matt (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR to add a validation step in the alias promotion pipeline. link PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/runtime/merge-validate-compat/987

jess (eng-sre): will prepare a short runbook entry: "If embeddings 500s spike after deploy, check alias compatibility and disable fallback for alias-region."

carol (support): customers confirmed reduced errors after 14:18 UTC. continuing to monitor.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated. page updated. Severity: Sev2. Duration (detect->mitigate): ~8 minutes.

omar (product): thanks team. we'll schedule a postmortem and cc affected account owners.

sara (oncall): I'm handing off to jess for follow-up. jess, you're now on the incident rotation owner for the postmortem. :handshake:

jess (eng-sre): ack. I'll sync with matt and carol and file the incident report.
